name: Mzieme Naga
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Marrison, Geoffrey E. 1967. The Classification of the Naga Languages of North-East India (phoneme data incl. Mzieme; cited on Glottolog mzie1235; not online)

sources.citation: Soppitt, C. A. 1885. A short account of the Kachcha Naga (Empeo) tribe in the North Cachar Hills, with an outline grammar. Shillong. §3 'Accents'.
sources.note: Has an accent rule (first-syllable default, suffix-driven shifts) but for Kachcha Naga/Empeo of North Cachar = Zeme proper (zeme1240), already recorded there; not a Mzieme description.

sources.citation: Ezung, Mimi Kevichüsa & Pangersenla Walling. 2021. Typology of the Naga Languages: A Pilot Study. Kohima: Tribal Research Institute, Govt. of Nagaland.
sources.note: Silent. Morphological/syntactic typology of 17 Nagaland languages including 'Zeliang (Zeme)' with an informant from Poilwa village, Peren district (the Mzieme area). No phonology; 'stress'/'accent' absent; 'tone' appears only in the bibliography.

sources.citation: Muchahary, Francis. 2019. The phonology and morphology of Zeme Naga. PhD thesis, Assam University, Silchar (Zeme of Dima Hasao, Assam).
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Silent: 0 hits for 'stress'/'accent' in the phonology chapter; three tones. Describes zeme1240 (Assam), lists Mzieme as a separate member of Burling's Zeme group (ch. 1).

sources.citation: Chanu, Sapam Sangita. 2017. A descriptive grammar of Zeme. PhD thesis, Assam University, Silchar.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Silent: 0 hits for 'stress'/'accent'; two tones. Describes zeme1240.

sources.citation: Raguibou, I. D. 2015. The comparative phonology of Zeme, Liangmai and Rongmei. PhD thesis, Assam University, Silchar. Ch. 3 (Zeme defined as spoken in Dima Hasao, Tamenglong, Senapati and Paren district of Nagaland).
sources.note: Silent: 0 hits for 'stress'/'accent' in ch. 3; §3.1.7 Tone: three contrastive tones in Zeme. Its 'Zeme' nominally includes the Peren (Mzieme) area but data are pooled Zeme.

sources.citation: Kapfo, Kedutso & Pauning Haikam. 2011. Zeme Folktales. Mysore: CIIL (with Textbook Section, Dept. of School Education, Govt. of Nagaland).
sources.note: Silent. English-language folktale collection with preface; no linguistic description.

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul (ed.). 2009. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 16th ed. Entry 'Naga, Mzieme' [nme].
sources.note: Silent. Location (Paren area, NE of Zeme), alternate name 'Northern Zeme', 'Different from Zeme Naga [nzm]', Bible 1992; no typology notes.

sources.citation: Burling, Robbins. 2003. The Tibeto-Burman languages of Northeastern India. In Thurgood & LaPolla (eds.), The Sino-Tibetan Languages. London: Routledge. 'Zeme group' section.
sources.note: Silent. Classification only: Zeme (15), Mzieme (29), Liangmai (18) 'particularly close', all Marrison's C-2.

sources.citation: Sreedhar, M. V. 1974. Naga Pidgin: A Sociolinguistic Study of Inter-lingual Communication Pattern in Nagaland. Mysore: CIIL.
sources.note: Silent on stress; identity only (p. 14): 'Mzieme, the North-Eastern dialect of Zemi is the main dialect of Zemi, spoken within the borders of Nagaland. It has two sub-dialects, viz., Paren and Njauna dialects.'

sources.citation: Evans, Jonathan. n.d. A survey of Tibeto-Burman phonological phenomena (Academia Sinica, draft).
sources.note: Silent on stress; Mzieme cited (via UPSID/PHOIBLE, ultimately Marrison 1967) for /ʍ/ as sole voiceless sonorant and prenasalised fricatives.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page mzie1235 and Wikipedia 'Mzieme language'.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology; Glottolog cites only Marrison 1967 (subclassification) and Campbell et al. 2022; Wikipedia cites only Ethnologue 18.

sources.citation: Halemane, Lingadevaru & Pauning Haikam. n.d. Adult Primer in Zeme. Mysore: CIIL.
sources.note: Silent. Literacy primer in Zeme orthography (Nagaland CIIL series); no pronunciation guide.

sources.citation: Namkung, Ju (ed.). 1996. Phonological Inventories of Tibeto-Burman Languages. STEDT Monograph Series 3. Berkeley: Center for Southeast Asia Studies, University of California. xxviii+507 pp. ISBN 0-944613-28-4. Entry 'Mzieme' (Kamarupan / Naga (Southwestern)), pp. 271-272, data source Marrison 1967 [GEM-CNL] pp. 359-360.

tone.quote: MZIEME / Data Source: Marrison 1967 [GEM-CNL] / Spoken in the Zeliang sub-district of the Kohima District of Nagaland and in a few villages of northwest Manipur. Marrison takes his lexical data from [GEM-Mzieme]. / Inventory: Marrison 1967 [GEM-CNL] (pages 359-360) / SYLLABLE CANON (C)V(V)(C) ... Marrison's charts on page 359 are incomplete. Additional information was extracted from the data. Mzieme has a rich system of prenasalization, including a series of prenasalized nasals. The prenasalization is probably syllabic.
tone.locator: pp. 271-272; no TONES section in the entry

sources.note: State-wise PLSI volumes carry short sketches of each scheduled tribal language with a sound-system note; the Nagaland Zeliang chapter would cover the Peren (Mzieme) variety.

sources.citation: Ezung, Mimi Kevichüsa. 2017. A general survey of tones in the Naga languages. Paper presented at the Workshop on Tones, CIIL Mysore / Centre for Naga Tribal Language Studies, Nagaland University.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Cited in Ezung & Walling 2021; a Nagaland-based survey of tone across Naga languages including Zeliang (Zeme of Peren = Mzieme) and the likeliest modern statement on suprasegmentals for this variety.

sources.citation: Marrison, Geoffrey E. 1967. The classification of the Naga languages of North East India. PhD thesis, SOAS, University of London, 2 vols (300+460 pp.). Mzieme = language no. 29, with phonological sketch and wordlist.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only work Glottolog links to Mzieme with phoneme data; its per-language phonological sketches are the one place a statement on Mzieme tone/stress is likely to exist (UPSID/PHOIBLE Mzieme inventory derives from it).

sources.citation: Any Nagaland University (Tenyidie/Naga Tribal Language Studies) MPhil/PhD on Zeliang phonology (none found on Shodhganga under 'Zeliang', 'Zemi', 'Mzieme', 'Peren').

sources.citation: Zeliang/Zeme school-language materials of the Textbook Section, Dept. of School Education, Govt. of Nagaland (Zeliang grammar/primer series used in Peren district).

sources.note: Ezung & Walling 2021 and Kapfo & Haikam 2011 show CIIL and the Nagaland textbook section produced Zeme (Nagaland) materials; a Zeliang grammar primer may include a pronunciation/accent note for the Mzieme variety.
